title: Training loss and sampler
goal:
Implement Algorithm 1 (one loss evaluation) and Algorithm 2 (sampling) with an epsilon-prediction model `eps_model(x, t)`.

`ddpm_loss(eps_model, x0, t, eps, alpha_bars)` builds $x_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,x_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,\epsilon$ and returns $\|\epsilon - \epsilon_\theta(x_t, t)\|^2$ (Equation 14), summed over the data dimensions and averaged over the batch. The model gets `x_t` and the integer array `t`, never `x_0`.

`sample(eps_model, shape, betas, rng, sigma="beta")` starts from $x_T \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$ and runs $t = T, \dots, 1$ with $x_{t-1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}\left(x_t - \frac{1-\alpha_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\epsilon_\theta(x_t, t)\right) + \sigma_t z$ (Algorithm 2, line 4). Here $z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$ for $t > 1$ and $z = 0$ for $t = 1$. Set $\sigma_t^2 = \beta_t$ when `sigma="beta"` and $\sigma_t^2 = \tilde\beta_t$ when `sigma="beta_tilde"` (Section 3.2). The sampler calls `eps_model(x, t)` with `t` as a single integer.
hints: Sum the squared error over the last axis, then average over the batch. Averaging over every entry divides the loss by the data dimension.
Draw the noise with `rng.standard_normal(shape)` and branch on `t > 1`. Adding noise at the last step leaves residual noise in the output.
The loop counts down: `for t in range(T, 0, -1)`. Read `betas[t - 1]` and `alpha_bars[t - 1]`.
For $\tilde\beta_t$ use $\bar\alpha_{t-1} = 1$ when $t = 1$. The noise is skipped there anyway.
